    27	## Identity and isolation
    28	
    29	The gateway persists the workspace, requester, original channel/thread,
    30	inbound message identifier, original goal and private worker source in the
    31	protected `.clanker-vault/requests.sqlite` coordinator database. The
    32	`transfers.reply_mode` and `task_state` columns distinguish channel work from
    33	legacy private handoffs. This state survives gateway/service restarts.
    34	
    35	Each channel task gets a fresh `profiles/task-<transfer-id>` execution home,
    36	native session database and browser context. Personal DM files, memories,
    37	history and browser profiles are not copied. The native agent skips personal
    38	memory, context files, SOUL, prefill and background review; middleware also
    39	rejects memory/session-search tools. Shared follow-ups cannot select or reuse
    40	the task home.
    41	
    42	Credentials remain encrypted in the requester's personal vault. Trusted fill
    43	and API handlers resolve owned or explicitly invited handles against that
    44	vault, validate the target origin and use the separate worker browser. Newly
    45	saved credentials go to the personal vault; one-time codes remain encrypted
    46	and single-use. The task home receives no credential-vault copy.
    47	
    48	A native `IsolatedGatewayTask` capability connects the worker to its result
    49	handler. It is never serialized into Slack input or session-source dictionaries.
    50	Only the durable, owner-validated coordinator resume attaches it. Membership,
    51	source fields, task state, served home and original destination are checked
    52	again during routing and publication.
    53	
    54	## Result publication and recovery
    55	
    56	Native streaming, interim replies, tool progress, task cards, voice and media
    57	egress are suppressed for this worker. The trusted login handler still sends
    58	forms privately. A model reply while a form is pending is not a final result.
    59	The form also records its originating gateway event, so that turn's waiting
    60	reply stays suppressed even if the form is saved before the reply or restart.
    61	
    62	The final text is encrypted into a SQLite outbox before optional vault reads or
    63	Slack I/O. Before publication the handler scrubs current owned/invited secret
    64	values and applies native redaction. If redaction or Slack fails, publication
    65	retries the retained answer. A persisted native completed reply can also be
    66	adopted after the coordinator-write crash gap without starting another agent
    67	turn. Publication validates current original-channel membership.

    70	via Slack `conversations.replies` to reconcile an acknowledgement lost before
    71	SQLite marks completion. The Slack app must have the relevant thread-history
    72	and write permissions. The same inbound message deduplicates its detour; a new
    73	message can create another task even when its text matches.

    76	does not provide exactly-once semantics for website mutations or purchases.

    80	
    81	`/stop`, `/new` and `/reset` in the original thread cancel that requester's
    82	linked forms and private worker, stop its browser contexts and invalidate
    83	pending result publication. Other members and other threads retain their tasks.

    85	browser contexts before removing the credential.

    88	cancels those workers and attempts cleanup for each home. Failed cleanup stays
    89	pending and blocks reuse; success for one home does not erase another home's
    90	marker. Provider cleanup attempts every recorded session even when an earlier
    91	session fails.

    99	pin and reapplies the complete patch stack idempotently.

    15	thread. Starting such a task authorizes sharing its requested result with that
    16	thread's audience. Sensitive task requests should start in a DM.
    17	
    18	People who can read the shared thread can read its messages and Clanker's
    19	published result. Reading or replying grants no access to the requester's vault,
    20	private conversations, browser cookies or worker. Another member's follow-up
    21	binds to that member's identity and authorized accounts. Account invitations
    22	remain explicit and revocable.
    23	
    24	Ordinary DM tasks and previously persisted private handoffs retain private
    25	results. The change applies to newly created channel task detours.
    26	
    27	## Identity and isolation
    28	
    29	The gateway persists the workspace, requester, original channel/thread,
    30	inbound message identifier, original goal and private worker source in the
    31	protected `.clanker-vault/requests.sqlite` coordinator database. The
    32	`transfers.reply_mode` and `task_state` columns distinguish channel work from
    33	legacy private handoffs. This state survives gateway/service restarts.
    34	
    35	Each channel task gets a fresh `profiles/task-<transfer-id>` execution home,
    36	native session database and browser context. Personal DM files, memories,
    37	history and browser profiles are not copied. The native agent skips personal
    38	memory, context files, SOUL, prefill and background review; middleware also
    39	rejects memory/session-search tools. Shared follow-ups cannot select or reuse
    40	the task home.
    41	
    42	Credentials remain encrypted in the requester's personal vault. Trusted fill
    43	and API handlers resolve owned or explicitly invited handles against that
    44	vault, validate the target origin and use the separate worker browser. Newly
    45	saved credentials go to the personal vault; one-time codes remain encrypted
    46	and single-use. The task home receives no credential-vault copy.
    47	
    48	A native `IsolatedGatewayTask` capability connects the worker to its result
    49	handler. It is never serialized into Slack input or session-source dictionaries.
    50	Only the durable, owner-validated coordinator resume attaches it. Membership,
    51	source fields, task state, served home and original destination are checked
    52	again during routing and publication.
    53	
    54	## Result publication and recovery
    55	
    56	Native streaming, interim replies, tool progress, task cards, voice and media
    57	egress are suppressed for this worker. The trusted login handler still sends
    58	forms privately. A model reply while a form is pending is not a final result.
    59	The form also records its originating gateway event, so that turn's waiting
    60	reply stays suppressed even if the form is saved before the reply or restart.
    61	
    62	The final text is encrypted into a SQLite outbox before optional vault reads or
    63	Slack I/O. Before publication the handler scrubs current owned/invited secret
    64	values and applies native redaction. If redaction or Slack fails, publication
    65	retries the retained answer. A persisted native completed reply can also be
    66	adopted after the coordinator-write crash gap without starting another agent
    67	turn. Publication validates current original-channel membership.
    68	
    69	Each result uses a stable `client_msg_id`. The handler pages the original thread
    70	via Slack `conversations.replies` to reconcile an acknowledgement lost before
    71	SQLite marks completion. The Slack app must have the relevant thread-history
    72	and write permissions. The same inbound message deduplicates its detour; a new
    73	message can create another task even when its text matches.
    74	
    75	An unfinished interrupted website operation may run again after restart. This
    76	does not provide exactly-once semantics for website mutations or purchases.
    77	Existing purchase approval and unknown-outcome rules still apply.
    78	
    79	## Stop and revocation
    80	
    81	`/stop`, `/new` and `/reset` in the original thread cancel that requester's
    82	linked forms and private worker, stop its browser contexts and invalidate
    83	pending result publication. Other members and other threads retain their tasks.
    84	Disconnect cancels the owner's outstanding tasks and clears their recorded
    85	browser contexts before removing the credential.
    86	
    87	An invited credential records every execution home that used it. Revocation
    88	cancels those workers and attempts cleanup for each home. Failed cleanup stays
    89	pending and blocks reuse; success for one home does not erase another home's
    90	marker. Provider cleanup attempts every recorded session even when an earlier
    91	session fails.
    92	
    93	## Integration and activation
    94	
    95	`runtime/vault/channel_tasks.py` owns task execution and publication;
    96	`channel_control.py` owns validated cleanup. Generic Hermes changes are recorded
    97	in `patches/hermes/channel-task-return.patch`; the runtime routing mirror has a
    98	separate upgrade patch. `scripts/apply-hermes-mods` verifies the audited Hermes
    99	pin and reapplies the complete patch stack idempotently.
   100	
   101	This acceptance covers text results with fixture Slack/model/provider execution,
   102	real profile provisioning, SQLite, encryption and native middleware. Attachment
   103	export and a real Slack/browser end-to-end run are still unverified. Live
   104	end-to-end acceptance requires a controlled owner task covering
   105	private login/code save, original-thread return, another member's follow-up and
   106	original-thread stop.
   107	
   108	The local Mac operator and existing Seatbelt/provider trust boundaries remain
   109	those documented in the [execution decision](2026-10-05-local-execution-boundary.md).
"}}

The extra profiles come from **one permanent Hermes profile per private task**.

- `runtime/vault/channel_tasks.py:111` creates `task-<transfer-id>` through native profile provisioning. The reason is separating a channel task from personal memory, conversation history and browser state.
- `runtime/slack_workspace.py:133` builds each as a full profile, including config, model authentication and `state.db`.
- `runtime/vault/store.py:310` deduplicates the same inbound task, but a new message can create another transfer/profile.
- `runtime/vault/store.py:482` only marks completion. There is **no retirement step** removing or archiving that task profile.
- `/stop` cleanup in `runtime/vault/channel_control.py:185` interrupts workers and clears browsers, but also leaves the Hermes profile.

The five base profiles are three personal contexts and two shared channels, documented in `verification/evidence/2026-10-05-browser-execution.md:15`. The persona migration did not create the other 31; it updated the existing fleet (`docs/decisions/2026-10-08-clanker-single-persona.md:29`).

Root’s verified breakdown, **5 base + 31 tasks; 27 completed, 1 cancelled, 3 active**, supports calling this accumulated task profiles caused by missing lifecycle cleanup. These are task records promoted into permanent profiles, rather than 36 different Clanker identities.
